Seminar Title:

Triarylamine-based fluorescent organic molecules for multifunctional applications, including sensing, white LEDs, and latent fingerprinting.

Seminar Type:

Progress Seminar

Department:

Chemistry

Speaker Name:

Anthem Tirkey ( Rollno : 523cy3004)

Speaker Type:

Student

Venue:

Seminar Room, chemistry department.

Date and Time:

18 Nov 2026 11 AM.

Contact:

Jaya Prakash Madda

Abstract:

Triarylamine-based fluorescent organic molecules, TBA-HZ and TBA-MN, were synthesized and developed for multifunctional molecular materials for chemical sensing, solid-state fluorescence modulation, and practical imaging/lighting applications. TBA-HZ enabled recognition and discrimination of chlorinated solvents and selective detection of picric acid via distinct fluorescence responses, while its solid-state aggregation could be modulated by metal-salt grinding. It also demonstrated potential for white-light-emitting applications. TBA-MN, a donor&ndash&pi&ndashacceptor molecule containing malononitrile acceptor units and a tri(biphenyl)amine donor core, exhibited solvatochromism and aggregation-induced emission, enabling selective Fe&sup3⁺ sensing with a low detection limit of 1.53 &microM. Metal-salt grinding further provided tunable solid-state fluorescence, while its strong emission enabled high-resolution latent fingerprint visualization. Overall, these studies demonstrate the versatility of triarylamine-based fluorescent molecular platforms for environmental sensing, solid-state photophysical modulation, optical materials, and forensic applications.
